breakfast.name: Socca (Chickpea Flatbread)
instructions: Mix chickpea flour with water, oil, salt
Pour into hot oiled pan
Bake at high heat until edges crisp
Cut into pieces
breakfast.description: Crispy chickpea flatbread — shared with neighboring Nice.

breakfast.name: Croissant et Café
instructions: Warm croissant
Serve with fresh espresso

breakfast.name: Pain au Chocolat (Viennoiserie)
ingredients: Store-bought or bakery pain au chocolat (croissant dough with dark chocolate)
instructions: Monaco is a tiny principality with no distinct agricultural tradition — French cuisine dominates
The morning bakery (boulangerie) is the Monaco breakfast institution
Pain au chocolat: croissant dough wrapped around a bar of dark chocolate
Eaten with espresso (café) or café au lait
The quality of Monaco's bakeries is exceptional — luxury clientele demand it
This is not a recipe that changes in Monaco — it's the same as anywhere in France
The Monaco context: eating this at a café table in Monte Carlo, with a view of the Mediterranean
The experience is the context, not the food itself
Monaco's small size (2.02 km²) means all food culture is essentially Nice and French Riviera
The principality's original food (Monégasque cuisine) is a small variation of Nice cuisine
breakfast.description: Monaco's French Riviera breakfast — pain au chocolat from the morning bakery, eaten with espresso at a café table with Mediterranean views. Monaco's food culture is essentially French Riviera (Nice) cuisine: the principality (2.02 km²) has no distinct agricultural tradition. Monégasque cuisine is a small variation of Niçois cooking.

breakfast.name: Socca (Chickpea Flatbread)
instructions: Mix chickpea flour with water and olive oil into a thin, smooth batter
Rest 30 minutes
Pour into a very hot, oiled cast iron pan — thin layer
Bake or broil until set and slightly charred on top — 8-10 minutes
Or: use a wood-fired oven (traditional Nice-Monaco method)
Cut into irregular pieces
Season with black pepper immediately from the oven — generously
Socca is Nice's (and by extension Monaco's) traditional street food
Made from chickpea flour — a legume flour that grows in the region
The slight char, the olive oil richness, and the black pepper is the complete flavor
Socca should be eaten immediately — it becomes rubbery as it cools
Street socca vendors serve it on paper, standing at the stall
breakfast.description: Monaco's (and Nice's) traditional chickpea flatbread — chickpea flour batter baked thin until charred on top in a very hot cast iron pan, cut irregularly and eaten immediately with black pepper. Socca is the French Riviera's street food with no parallel elsewhere in France. Must be eaten immediately — it becomes rubbery as it cools.

lunch.name: Barbagiuan (Fried Pastries)
ingredients: Filling: Swiss chard, ricotta, onion, Parmesan
instructions: Make dough, rest
Cook chard and onion, mix with ricotta and Parmesan
Fill dough rounds, seal
Deep fry until golden
lunch.description: Monaco's national dish — fried pastries filled with chard and ricotta.

lunch.name: Stocafi (Dried Cod Stew)
instructions: Soak stockfish 2 days
Sauté onion, garlic
Add tomatoes, potatoes, olives, herbs
Add fish, simmer 45 min
lunch.description: Stockfish stewed with tomatoes and olives — Monégasque comfort.

lunch.name: Salade Niçoise
ingredients: Tuna (fresh seared or good quality canned in oil)
Lettuce (butter lettuce or no lettuce — this is a debate)
Vinaigrette: olive oil, red wine vinegar, Dijon
Boiled potato (another debate — purists say no)
instructions: The Niçoise salad has passionate debates about its 'correct' composition
The traditional Niçoise (from Nice, a short drive from Monaco) has no cooked vegetables except egg
No potato, no cooked green beans — this is the purist position
Monaco has no distinct Niçoise salad position — it accepts the Nice version
Arrange all components on a plate — this is composed, not tossed
The vinaigrette is drizzled, not tossed
Each component visible and distinct
The anchovy gives salt — with it, no extra salt needed
The combination: tuna-egg-olive-tomato-anchovy — the Mediterranean flavors together
Salade niçoise is France's most significant salad contribution to world cuisine
lunch.description: Monaco's French Riviera composed salad — tuna, hard-boiled eggs, Niçoise olives, anchovy, tomato, and green beans in a vinaigrette, arranged (never tossed). The salade Niçoise debate (potato or no? cooked vegetables or raw only?) has passionate adherents. Monaco follows Nice's traditional position. The combination of tuna-egg-anchovy-olive is the Mediterranean distilled.

lunch.name: Pissaladière (Onion Tart)
ingredients: Onions (enormous quantity — 1 kg for a small tart)
instructions: Cook onions: slice very thin, fry in olive oil over low heat 30-40 minutes
The onions must caramelize completely — from sharp to sweet, from white to golden-brown
This is the critical step — undercooked onions ruin pissaladière
Roll pizza-type dough thin, rectangular
Spread caramelized onions generously over the dough
Arrange anchovies in a diamond or cross-hatch pattern on top
Press olives into each diamond/section
Bake at 220°C until crust is cooked and everything is fragrant
Pissaladière is Nice-Monaco's pizza equivalent — the regional flatbread
The caramelized onion base is what makes it — sweet, rich, mellow
The salty anchovy and olive against the sweet onion is the flavor architecture
lunch.description: Monaco's onion flatbread — bread dough topped with a deep layer of 40-minute-caramelized onions, crisscross anchovy fillets, and Niçoise olives. The French Riviera's pizza equivalent. The caramelized onion base must be completely sweet and golden — this takes 40 minutes minimum. The salty anchovy against the sweet caramelized onion is the pissaladière's defining contrast.

dinner.name: Bouillabaisse
instructions: Make fish broth with bones
Sauté fennel, onion, garlic
Add tomatoes, saffron, orange peel
Add firm fish first, delicate last
Serve broth with croutons and rouille, fish on side

dinner.name: Fougasse Monégasque (Sweet Flatbread)
instructions: Mix dough with orange blossom water
Let rise 1 hour
Shape, top with sugar
Bake at 180°C 20 min
dinner.description: Orange blossom-scented flatbread — traditionally for feast days.

dinner.name: Bouillabaisse (Marseille Fish Stew)
ingredients: Mixed rockfish (essential: at least 3-4 species including rascasse/scorpionfish)
Saffron (generous — it colors the broth golden)
instructions: The bouillabaisse is technically from Marseille — but Monaco on the French Riviera shares the tradition
The essential fish: rascasse (scorpionfish) — non-negotiable in the traditional version
Fry aromatics in olive oil: onion, leek, fennel, tomato, garlic
Add orange zest — this is the Provençal signature that distinguishes bouillabaisse from other fish soups
Add fish in order of cooking time — firm fish first, delicate last
Pour saffron-infused broth over
Cook quickly — the 'bouillie' technique: rolling boil to emulsify the oil
Strain broth, serve in two courses: broth first with rouille croutons, then fish
The rouille is the companion: garlic-saffron aioli spread on croutons, which float in the broth
Bouillabaisse is one of the world's great fish soups
Orange zest + saffron + rascasse: the irreducible Provençal combination
dinner.description: Monaco's Provençal fish stew — the French Riviera's most complex seafood dish: multiple species of rockfish (rascasse essential), saffron, orange zest (the Provençal signature), and olive oil emulsified at a rolling boil. Served in two courses: saffron broth first with rouille croutons, then the fish. Orange zest + saffron + rascasse is the irreducible Provençal combination.

dinner.name: Daube à la Niçoise (Beef Stew with Olives)
ingredients: Beef (chuck or brisket — tough cuts that need long braising)
Red wine (Provençal — Côtes du Rhône or similar)
Orange zest, bay leaf, thyme, rosemary
instructions: Marinate beef overnight in red wine with aromatics — the marinade is the foundation
The next day: brown beef pieces in olive oil
Remove beef, fry onion, carrot, garlic in the same fat
Add back beef, the wine marinade, tomatoes
Add orange zest (the Niçoise/Provençal signature)
Braise in a low oven (160°C) for 2.5-3 hours
The long braising dissolves collagen — the sauce becomes rich and glossy
Add olives in the last 30 minutes — they soften but keep texture
Daube niçoise is the French Riviera's beef stew — the orange zest and olives distinguish it
Different from Burgundy boeuf bourguignon (no olives, different herbs)
Served with pasta (Nice tradition) or mamaliga — the Italian influence from nearby
dinner.description: Monaco's braised beef stew — overnight-marinated beef braised for hours in Provençal red wine with Niçoise olives and orange zest (the French Riviera signature). The orange zest and olives distinguish daube niçoise from Burgundy's boeuf bourguignon. After 3 hours of braising the collagen dissolves and the sauce becomes deeply glossy. Served with pasta — Nice's Italian cultural influence.

dinner.name: Stockfish à la Niçoise (Salt Cod)
ingredients: Salt cod (stockfish — very thick, desalted over 2-3 days in cold water changes)
instructions: Desalt the cod: 2-3 days in cold water, changing water 3 times daily
The fish should be completely fresh-tasting with only a mild salt flavor
After desalting: break into large pieces
Fry onion, garlic in olive oil with anchovies (they melt into the oil)
Add tomatoes — cook down
Add capers, olives, thyme
Add cod pieces — fold in gently
Braise 20-25 minutes — the cod should flake but not disintegrate
Stockfish (bacalhà / morue) is Monaco's/Nice's Friday dish
The Catholic tradition of no-meat Friday kept salt cod as the alternative protein
Monaco's Friday stockfish dish is the last remnant of the pre-refrigeration preserved food tradition
dinner.description: Monaco's Friday salt cod — desalted over 2-3 days, braised with tomatoes, black olives, anchovies, and capers. The Catholic no-meat Friday tradition kept salt cod (bacalhà) as the preserved-fish alternative. Monaco's stockfish preparation is the French Riviera version: heavy on olive oil, tomato, and olives — very different from Portuguese or Scandinavian salt cod traditions.

snacks.name: Pissaladière (Onion Tart)
instructions: Make pizza dough
Caramelize onions slowly with thyme
Spread on dough
Top with anchovies and olives
Bake at 200°C until crisp
snacks.description: Caramelized onion tart with anchovies and olives.

snacks.name: Fougasse (Provençal Flatbread)
ingredients: Olive oil (in the dough and on top)
Optional: olives, anchovies, herbs (rosemary, thyme) baked in
instructions: Make an olive-oil enriched yeasted dough
Let rise 1 hour
Roll into a flat oval — thinner than focaccia
Cut decorative slashes in the dough — the traditional ladder or leaf pattern
The slashes expand during baking — they're structural and aesthetic
Drizzle with olive oil, press optional additions (olives, rosemary) into the surface
Bake at 220°C until golden and crispy at the edges — the center is chewier
Fougasse is Provence's flatbread — Monaco's bakeries sell it
Different from Italian focaccia (the slashes, the shape, the less-oily nature)
The olive oil-enriched dough with rosemary is the basic version
Sweet fougasse exists too: with orange blossom water and sugar
snacks.description: Monaco's Provençal flatbread — olive oil-enriched yeasted dough slashed in a ladder pattern and baked until the edges are crispy while the center stays chewy. The decorative slashes are both structural (allowing even baking) and aesthetic. Different from Italian focaccia in shape, slash pattern, and oil quantity. Monaco's bakeries sell fougasse alongside croissants.

snacks.name: Panisses (Chickpea Fritters)
instructions: Cook chickpea flour in water with olive oil and salt — stir continuously
Like making polenta but with chickpea flour
The mixture thickens and begins to pull from the sides
Pour into a flat, oiled tray — smooth to 1 cm thickness
Refrigerate until completely firm (1+ hours)
Unmold and cut into rectangles or squares
Fry in olive oil until golden and crispy on all sides
The exterior should be very crispy; the interior smooth and creamy
Panisses are Nice-Monaco's fried chickpea cake — similar to Genoese panissa
The chickpea-olive oil combination is the Ligurian-Provençal overlap
Eaten as a snack, a street food, or an appetizer
snacks.description: Monaco's fried chickpea cakes — chickpea flour cooked until thick, set in a flat tray, cut, and fried until extremely crispy outside with a creamy interior. Related to Genoese panissa and more distantly to Sicilian panelle. The crispy chickpea exterior-creamy interior contrast is the panisse pleasure. Monaco sits at the Ligurian-Provençal overlap, and panisses show that geography.

snacks.name: Fruits Confits (Candied Fruits)
ingredients: Various fruits: apricots, figs, clementines, pears, cherries
instructions: Fruit candying is a specialty of the Nice/Riviera region
The process: gradually replace fruit moisture with sugar syrup over many days
Day 1: simmer fruit in light syrup
Day 2: remove fruit, add more sugar to syrup, re-simmer fruit
Repeat 5-7 times — each time the sugar concentration increases
The fruit becomes translucent and preserved in crystallized sugar
The final fruit is intensely sweet, jewel-colored, and shelf-stable for months
Nice is world-famous for its fruits confits (candied fruits)
Monaco's confiseries sell candied fruits as luxury gifts
The technique developed in the medieval period — sugar preservation as luxury
Clementines from the Riviera, apricots from Provence — the specific regional fruits matter
snacks.description: Monaco's luxury candy — fruit preserved through repeated immersion in progressively concentrated sugar syrup over 5-7 days until translucent and jewel-like. Nice is world-famous for fruits confits. Monaco's confiseries sell them as luxury gifts. The technique dates to medieval sugar preservation. Regional fruits (Riviera clementines, Provençal apricots) make the best ones.

desserts.name: Tourte de Blettes (Swiss Chard Pie)
instructions: Make sweet pastry
Chop chard, mix with eggs, sugar, pine nuts, raisins, cheese
Fill pastry, top with pastry
Bake at 180°C 40 min
Dust with sugar
desserts.description: A sweet-savory chard pie — Monégasque tradition.

desserts.name: Tarte aux Fraises (Strawberry Tart)
instructions: Make pâte sablée: flour, butter, egg yolk, sugar, salt
Press into tart ring, blind bake until golden and crisp
Make crème pâtissière: milk, eggs, sugar, cornstarch, vanilla, butter
Cool completely
Fill tart shell with pastry cream — spread evenly
Arrange strawberries on top — points up, in concentric circles
Brush with warm apricot glaze — it gives the glossy finish and prevents browning
French pastry technique in its most elegant form
Monaco's patisseries produce some of the finest examples in the world
The strawberry tart is the spring French patisserie icon — Riviera strawberries in April-May
desserts.description: Monaco's spring patisserie — buttery tart shell filled with vanilla pastry cream, topped with perfectly arranged strawberries and glazed with apricot. French patisserie technique at its most elegant. Monaco's patisseries are among the finest in the world (serving an exceptionally wealthy clientele). Riviera strawberries in April-May are exceptional.

desserts.name: Crème Brûlée
ingredients: Sugar (in the custard + more for the crust)
instructions: Infuse heavy cream with vanilla bean — heat until steaming, cool slightly
Whisk egg yolks with sugar until pale
Slowly pour warm cream into egg mixture — tempering to avoid scrambling
Add optional orange zest — the Riviera version
Strain into ramekins
Bake in a water bath (bain-marie) at 150°C — the water bath prevents cracking
Bake until set with a slight jiggle in the center — 35-40 minutes
Refrigerate until completely cold — overnight is ideal
Sprinkle sugar generously on top
Blowtorch (or broiler) the sugar until deeply caramelized — dark amber
The crack of the caramelized sugar crust is the crème brûlée sound
The contrast: cold, silky custard beneath a hot, crackable sugar crust
desserts.description: Monaco's custard classic — silky vanilla cream baked in a water bath until just set, chilled, then topped with sugar caramelized to a glass-hard crust with a blowtorch. The crack of the crust reveals cold custard beneath. The temperature and texture contrast (hot crackable sugar / cold silky custard) is the crème brûlée experience.

drinks.name: Pastis
instructions: Pour pastis over ice
Add cold water (turns cloudy)

drinks.name: Rosé Wine
instructions: Serve well chilled
Pair with seafood

drinks.name: Rosé de Provence (Wine)
ingredients: Provençal rosé (Côtes de Provence, Bandol, or Bouches-du-Rhône)
instructions: Provence is the world capital of rosé wine — 88% of Provence's wine production is rosé
The pale, barely-pink Provence rosé is a deliberate style — 'saignée' method or direct pressing
Served cold — 8-10°C
Provence rosé is dry, pale, Grenache-forward with herbal, strawberry notes
It defines the French Riviera summer
Monaco sits in Provence territory — Provence rosé is the default summer wine
Served at every Monaco terrace, beach club, and restaurant
The pale pink in a chilled glass is the visual signature of summer on the Riviera
Rosé de Provence is now the world's most-exported rosé category
The 'pale and Provençal' aesthetic has influenced rosé production worldwide
drinks.description: Monaco's summer wine — dry, pale Provençal rosé served cold. Provence produces 88% of France's rosé and has defined what 'rosé' means globally: pale, dry, Grenache-forward. Monaco on the French Riviera is rosé territory by geography. A chilled glass of pale pink rosé on a terrace overlooking the Mediterranean is Monaco's drink.
